import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from io import StringIO

# Data provided by the user
data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(StringIO(data))

# Set a style for better aesthetics
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a scatter plot to visualize relationships between key numerical and categorical features
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='brand',
    size='weight_grams', # Represent weight by marker size
    sizes=(100, 1000),  # Range for marker sizes
    style='sensor_type', # Represent sensor type by marker style
    palette='viridis', # Color palette for brands
    edgecolor='black',
    alpha=0.8
)

# Add text labels for model_year next to each point for additional context
# Adjusting text position slightly to avoid overlap with markers
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    plt.text(row['megapixels'] * 1.01, row['price_usd'] * 1.01, f"{row['model_year']}",
             horizontalalignment='left', size='small', color='dimgray', weight='semibold')

# Set plot title and labels
plt.title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels, by Brand, Sensor Type, Weight, and Model Year', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Megapixels', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=12)

# Improve legend placement to avoid overlapping with data points
plt.legend(bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0, title='Camera Attributes')

# Adjust layout to prevent labels/legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png')

# Close the plot to free up memory
plt.close()
